missiondescription.text: NexusSerialized, 4D7DCA174961531FE2406ABEAABDBAAA, People (capitalists) will try to convince you that currency exchange came about as a natural evolution of bartering, but that's not true. In sufficiently small, non-imperialist communities – communes, one might say – bartering of both goods and favors could have remained the primary means of transaction in perpetuity were it not for angry and greedy outsiders with big sticks. There are small communities in the East that still work like this; every household intentionally puts themselves into debt with every other household, so they all have a social justification for, and personal investment in, taking care of one another. Bartering by nature is an ambiguous value exchange which requires direct interaction between both parties and is thus more personal and (hypothetically) equitable. Anyway, this quest is like the one from that game where the twink gets eaten by a fish.
